messages.subject: hmc_refactor Questions
parts:
Two questions as I finalize the refactoring:

1) Before I had no persistent storage, so that each transition of the Markov chain would take in a sample and then return a new sample. I just added some persistent storage for a few reasons, so now the chains could theoretically just generate new samples from the internally stored point (as is currently done in master). Anyone have any preferences? The only trouble with the latter is that it would be hard to enforce across all samplers since they'd have different internal storage.

2) I was hoping to make shared data like mass matrices static to avoid extraneous memory allocation (possibly an issue for dense mass matrices and big models). The only problem is that I can't instantiate such an object with a dynamic size. Are there any tricks besides instantiating it to zero and then resizing it in a constructor?

-Mike

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] hmc_refactor Questions
parts:
On 3/30/13 9:07 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> Two questions as I finalize the refactoring:
>
> 1) Before I had no persistent storage, so that each transition of the Markov chain would take in a sample and then return a new sample. I just added some persistent storage for a few reasons, so now the chains could theoretically just generate new samples from the internally stored point (as is currently done in master). Anyone have any preferences? The only trouble with the latter is that it would be hard to enforce across all samplers since they'd have different internal storage.

What are you storing and in what object?

Is this so you don't have to compute quantities like H again for
new samples? If so, can these values be stored in the sample rather
than in the sampler so that the iterator can be something like:

sample sampler.next(const sample& last_sample);

> 2) I was hoping to make shared data like mass matrices static to avoid extraneous memory allocation (possibly an issue for dense mass matrices and big models). The only problem is that I can't instantiate such an object with a dynamic size. Are there any tricks besides instantiating it to zero and then resizing it in a constructor?

Are you sure you mean static, and if so, why static?
What are the thread safety implications? And what is the
alternative? (Static inits are very problematic in C++;
at the very least you should understand the basic singleton
pattern implementation in C++.)

The worst part of the entire Stan math design is the
way statics are used for the auto-diff stack. This destroys
thread safety and to get it back the static variables need
to be made thread local, which provides a pretty substantial
slowdown (about 15% in uncontended access in my measurements of
a year or two ago).

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] hmc_refactor Questions
parts: > What are you storing and in what object?

Each HMC sampler has an internal phase space point, containing the position, momentum, potential, and gradient, as a member. The advantage of having this as a member is that the sampler can be equipped with write functions that can be called after the sample has been generated, allowing easy printing of the detailed HMC data for diagnostics. In master this information is lost, requiring a diagnostic to modify the sampler::next member itself.

> Is this so you don't have to compute quantities like H again for
> new samples? If so, can these values be stored in the sample rather
> than in the sampler so that the iterator can be something like:
>
> sample sampler.next(const sample& last_sample);

That is exactly how I have it coded in the refactor right now (the input last_sample is really only used to initialize the internal storage, which ends up being redundant when the internal state and last_sample are consistent). In master, however, you just call sample (sample = sampler.next() ) assuming that the internal state of the sampler is correct (which is a fine assumption for a Markov chain).

> Are you sure you mean static, and if so, why static?
> What are the thread safety implications? And what is the
> alternative? (Static inits are very problematic in C++;
> at the very least you should understand the basic singleton
> pattern implementation in C++.)

Yeah, thread safety would be a concern.

Here's the issue: where do you put the (mass) metric? Do you store it in ps_point and duplicate the storage? This is more appropriate for R-HMC where the value of the metric is unique to each point, but then you need m * n^{2} storage, which can quickly become infeasible for large models. Or do you put a single metric in the sampler itself? This makes the sampler stateful (and fragments the state between ps_point and the sampler) and also has the same thread safety issues as you note above. I wasn't thinking about thread safety, and trying to use static to unify the state information without duplicating the actual memory.

Any thoughts?
